survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 country factsheet reports descriptive and trend statistics from the OECD PISA 2022 Database rather than estimating a custom student-level model. The underlying PISA sampling design is complex (students nested in schools, with stratification and clustering), so OECD analyses typically rely on PISA sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and correct standard errors. This factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the precise implementation details are not recoverable from the text provided. For users re-analyzing PISA microdata, the recommended approach is to apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the OECD PISA database documentation when computing means, proportions, and confidence intervals.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Latvia factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Latvia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to 2018. It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and gaps across socio-economic status and gender, using OECD PISA 2022 Database tables. The assessment uses two two-hour subject tests with rotated booklets, and students complete a background questionnaire while school principals complete a school questionnaire. The note also highlights special circumstances: PISA 2022 was delayed from 2021 due to COVID-19, and Latvia excluded more students than in 2018 (notably remote/virtual schooling), which may bias estimates. No student-level machine learning models are estimated in this factsheet; it is intended for policy interpretation of descriptive benchmarks and equity patterns.
